text:
sara: seeing a dozen attach failures in eu-west3 over the last 20m, all nodes show a spike in read errors during janitor scrubs. any quick wins?

mike: can you paste a sample of the node logs?

sara: pasted below from node-gnode-43 around 15:12
```
[15:12:03] scrubber: start pass id=7 target=/scratch
[15:12:07] nvme: read failed LBA=0x1a2f3b4c count=8 rc=-5
[15:12:07] nvme: remap triggered badblock=0x1a2f3b4c
[15:12:07] containerd: attach: failed to open backing file: EIO
[15:12:09] scrubber: rate=250MB/s concurrency=12
```

raj: interesting — concurrency 12 seems high for those small NVMe types in eu-west3. scrub bursts + reclaim cause IOPS starvation, then kernel surfaces read errors.

elaine: +1. we've seen remap storms before when the scrub overlaps with heavy prefetch from the ML batch jobs.

infra-bot: alert: node-gnode-43 disk read error rate 120/min (threshold 50) — created incident INC-4871

mike: quick mitigation: lower scrub concurrency and pause scrub on nodes with >50 read errs/min. can someone roll a hotfix to janitor config?

sara: i'll patch the cron to set concurrency=4 and add an early-exit if read_errs>30. testing on canary now (gnode-43 -> gnode-44 group).

josh: also recommend throttling snapshot reclaim during scrub windows. snapshot churn + scrub = perfect storm.

mike: for the medium term we should: 1) add adaptive scrub rate (based on iops headroom), 2) emit metric scrub_io_utilization, 3) change attach logic to retry-migrate to another local if EIO seen.

elaine: +1 on attach fallback. current behavior kills the pod. fallback to compatible node with >80% free iops would avoid customer impact.

raj: created a short runbook snippet for oncall:
```
- If node shows read_err > 50/min: sudo systemctl stop janitor-scrub
- Reduce concurrency: echo 4 > /etc/janitor/scrub_concurrency
- Trigger temporary allocation hold: /usr/local/bin/alloc-hold --node $NODE --until 10m
- Postmortem ticket: link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4871
```

sara: can we apply hold on eu-west3 as a whole while we stabilize? capacity hit but prevents attach flaps.

mike: ok to apply a short 30m hold only for batch-provisioning pool. ops, can you run alloc-hold for pool=batch-eu-west3 for 30m?

elaine: running now. also kicked off a firmware-health scan (non-disruptive) across the canaries. results ETA 18m.

infra-bot: action: alloc-hold applied to pool=batch-eu-west3 by elaine; duration=30m

josh: one more note — we'll need to tune our alerting to correlate scrub windows with read error spikes so we don't page on expected maintenance. add a suppression rule for scrub-maint windows but only if scrub concurrency <6.

mike: thanks team. next steps assigned: sara (patch janitor cron + canary validation), raj (runbook + alert suppression), josh (attach fallback design), elaine (alloc-hold + firmware scan). update INC-4871 with findings. :thumbsup:

sara: will update in 20m with canary results. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
